scenes.text: AI agents can now spend real money. They buy data, tools, and help from other agents. All on their own.
So how much should we let them spend? Most people pick a fixed limit. Say, fifty dollars a day.
scenes.cap: So how much should we let them spend? Most people pick a fixed limit. Say, $50 _ a day.

scenes.text: But that number is just a guess. A great agent runs out, and turns customers away. A bad agent wastes all of it, every single day. And if a thief steals the agent's key, the thief gets all of it too.
This is Kibble. Like treats for a puppy, the agent earns its spending, one piece at a time.
The agent's money sits in a locked box, on the blockchain. The agent can't open it. It can only ask the box to pay.
The box gives it a small tray to spend from. And the tray refills only when a real customer pays.
Anything extra goes straight into the owner's safe. The agent can never touch it.
When the agent makes money, its tray grows. When it loses money, the tray shrinks. The limit is earned, step by step.
And when things go wrong, the box hits the brakes by itself. Healthy. Watch. Braked. Paused. Nobody has to be watching.
The owner sets just one number: the most they are willing to lose in a week. Kibble works out the rest.
We put it to the test on the Q Day Ayvum testnet, a real blockchain. Two agents. Same code, same customers. One with a fixed limit, one with Kibble.
scenes.cap: We put it to the test on the QDay _ Aevum testnet, a real blockchain. Two agents. Same code, same customers. One with a fixed limit, one with Kibble.

scenes.text: On a busy day, both agents served every customer. Kibble's limit grew, and the profit went to the owner's safe.
On a losing day, every sale lost money. The fixed agent kept paying, again and again. Kibble stopped itself, seventy seconds after the price jump.
scenes.cap: On a losing day, every sale lost money. The fixed agent kept paying, again and again. Kibble stopped itself, 70 seconds after the price jump.

scenes.text: Then we handed a thief the agent's key. With the fixed limit, the thief kept spending, and nothing stopped it. With Kibble, the thief got nothing. The box locked itself in two seconds.
scenes.cap: Then we handed a thief the agent's key. With the fixed limit, the thief kept spending, and nothing stopped it. With Kibble, the thief got nothing. The box locked itself in 2 seconds.

scenes.text: These are real recordings, not a mock-up. Every payment and every refusal is written on chain. And anyone can try it, in the playground.
Behind it: one hundred and eighty-one tests. And the worst case is never a guess. It's a number anyone can read, at any moment.
scenes.cap: Behind it: 181 _ _ _ tests. And the worst case is never a guess. It's a number anyone can read, at any moment.

scenes.text: A fixed limit is a guess. Kibble's limit is earned. Don't give your agent a budget. Let it earn one.
